messages:
alex: heads up — got a support ticket from Acme Corp: p95 for /v1/generate with opal-2-extended jumped from ~120ms to ~480ms after yesterday's model add. customer seeing user-visible lag.

maria: ugh, saw alerts on metrics. Is this the new Opal rollout? which revision did we push to hosted catalog?

jordan: pushed opal-2-extended:v1.2.0 at 02:10 UTC, canary to 5% then 100% over 30m. no error spikes but latency did creep on long-seq workloads.

eng-runtime: looking at traces — root cause looks like tokenization step now doing extra normalization pass for emoji/CJK which doubles tokenization time on sequences >8k tokens. kv-cache hits unaffected but per-request preproc is heavy.

alex: customer repro steps: single HTTP request with large context (~12k tokens) + generate 256 tokens. sending example curl now.

alex: ```bash
curl -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -d '{"model":"opal-2-extended","input":"<12k chars>...","max_tokens":256}'
```

support-lead: can we reproduce internally on staging? if so we need a mitigation ASAP (canary rollback or transient throttling).

maria: repro'd on staging — p95 ~420ms vs opal-1.9 ~110ms for same payload. I captured a flamegraph, attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/xxxxx (stack shows tokenizer.normalize_unicode heavy).

eng-runtime: confirmed. The tokenizer change was intended to improve normalization for multilingual text but it added an O(n) regex pass that scales poorly with long sequences. Patch ready to remove expensive path for requests flagged as long-context.

sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-042, severity: high, affected: hosted api p95 for generate on opal-2-extended.

jordan: short-term options: 1) rollback opal-2-extended to v1.1.8, 2) add routing rule: route requests with content-length > 64k to opal-1.9, 3) enable per-request short-circuit for normalization (fast-path).

customer-ops: Acme needs a timeline. they said they hit this in prod and will throttle users if latency remains.

eng-runtime: quick mitigation plan: enable runtime flag disable_multilang_normalize for hosted until patch lands. that requires a config flip and can be staged per-tenant. risk: slightly different tokenization for some edge-cases.

support-lead: proceed with config flip for Acme only, and schedule a global rollback if any other major customers show impact. who can flip?

maria: I can push the per-tenant flag — will do Canary on Acme account now.

maria: flipped for Acme at 02:55 UTC — waiting 5m for metrics.

jordan: metrics look good — Acme p95 dropped to 130ms within two minutes. no errors.

eng-runtime: deploying patch to remove regex path now, will cut a hotfix build (v1.2.1) and canary to 10% for 15m before full rollout.

devex: note for docs — add release note about normalization option and potential perf tradeoffs for long-context workloads.

customer-ops: told Acme we'll keep the tenant flag on and coordinate a scheduled update. they asked for a rollback note for their internal ops.

support-lead: follow-ups: (1) postmortem draft, (2) add automated long-context perf tests to onboarding pipeline, (3) add telemetry to detect tokenization anomalies per model. assign owners?

alex: I'll own the customer comms and confirm flag duration.

eng-runtime: I'll own hotfix and perf tests.

maria: I'll write the canary playbook for per-tenant config flips.

support-lead: thanks — mark INC-2026-042 as mitigated for now. will keep thread open until hotfix fully rolled out. :thumbsup:
